scraped.scraped_description: The updated FME 2.0 offers very practical suggestions on how to engage civil society and affected communities in AI development to support platforms and AI developers in creating rights-based products.

name: Framework for Meaningful Engagement 2.0
tagline: Practical suggestions on how to engage civil society and affected communities in AI development to support platforms and AI developers in creating rights-based products
sdg_alignment: SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
policy_outcomes: Adoption by Amsterdam city government for AI governance
outcome_methodology: Case study documentation; pilot implementation tracking
published_performance_metrics: Framework adoption metrics; stakeholder feedback documentation
documented_limitations: Framework is guidance-based rather than prescriptive
Implementation outcomes depend on organizational commitment
curation_criteria: Multi-stakeholder consultation; rights-based approach; practical applicability
disparity_tracking: Framework addresses equity and inclusion in AI development; focuses on affected communities and marginalized groups
community_ownership: High - co-created with 300+ stakeholders from civil society, private sector, and public service
ai_involvement: Framework for meaningful engagement in AI development; pilot with Discord's Safety Machine Learning team; pilot with Amsterdam's image recognition service (scan bikes)
political_relevance_summary: Framework for Meaningful Engagement 2.0 addresses civic technology. Practical suggestions on how to engage civil society and affected communities in AI development to support platforms and AI developers in creating rights-based products.

movement_building_utility.notes: Provides technical infrastructure that other civic tools or services build upon.

generalizability_notes: Highly generalizable; already deployed across multiple countries. Open-source codebase facilitates replication.
